abstract: The ability to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) through illumination of photosensitizers provides a powerful means to manipulate cellular function with high spatial and temporal resolution. Here, we present a chemogenetic light-activatable ROS generator based on the FAST technology. By leveraging the heavy atom effect, we engineered chromophores, called ROSgen, that can both fluoresce and produce ROS when bound to FAST variants and exposed to light. Photosensitization is strictly dependent on the addition of the ROSgen, allowing for on-demand activated and targeted photomanipulation. We demonstrate that this chemogenetic light-activatable ROS generator enables to selectively perturb the function of organelles such as mitochondria, inactivate proteins or induce localized oxidative DNA damage, demonstrating its versatility as molecular tool for manipulating cellular processes with high spatial and temporal control.
